summary: This PR adds a nightly and per-run workflow, plus a Python script, that copy AI Review run records onto a `stats` branch and add one line per run to runs.jsonl. The overall design works. The main problem is the nightly backfill: it downloads the artifacts of every past run before checking whether that run is already recorded, so it gets slower each day and will eventually hit the 10-minute job timeout. Two smaller issues: one bad run stops the whole batch, and a compiled .pyc file is committed by mistake.

accepted.title: Nightly backfill downloads every past run again and will eventually time out
accepted.whatGoesWrong: With no run IDs given, the script lists up to 500 completed AI Review runs. For each one it calls `gh run view` and downloads all of its artifacts, and only then checks whether that run attempt is already recorded. After a few weeks of reviews, the nightly job spends minutes downloading data it already has, and it will pass the job's 10-minute timeout.
accepted.whyItMatters: Commit and push only happen after the script finishes. A timed-out job therefore records nothing, so the backfill that is meant to catch missed runs stops working, and every run burns CI minutes.
accepted.howToFix: Check runs.jsonl before any network call. Skip a run ID whose attempts are all already recorded, for example by comparing against the run's `attempt` from `gh run list --json databaseId,attempt,status`. Also stop at runs older than the artifact retention window.

accepted.title: One bad run stops every other run in the batch from being saved
accepted.whatGoesWrong: `gh run view` uses `check=True`, and the record file is read with an unguarded `json.loads`. If one run can't be viewed (a transient API error, or a deleted run) or its record JSON is truncated, the script crashes. That happens before anything is added to runs.jsonl. The nightly backfill then hits the same run every night.
accepted.whyItMatters: A single broken run can stop all stats collection until someone steps in by hand.
accepted.howToFix: Wrap each run's processing in try/except. Log the failure and skip that run so the other runs are still recorded and pushed.

rejected.title: A compiled Python cache file is committed
rejected.whatGoesWrong: The PR adds a local `__pycache__/*.pyc` file built by Python 3.14. CI never uses it; Python just rebuilds the cache. It will go stale as soon as the script is edited.
rejected.whyItMatters: It is a stale binary in the repo that clutters diffs and may confuse readers.
rejected.howToFix: Delete the file and add `__pycache__/` to .gitignore.
rejected.reason: file is not part of this PR's changes
